text.p: Hurricane Fran is expected to cause a storm surge of 12-16 feet as it makes landfall tonight along the upper South Carolina coast or the lower North Carolina coast. Maximum winds at the time of landfall should be 120-130 mph. This combination should lead to severe and widespread damage to coastal property. Rainfall of 5-10 inches and possibly higher is expected well inland across North Carolina and also Virginia and northern South Carolina with this system. These areas can expect widespread and severe flooding with a considerable amount of damage. Winds through the interior will also cause damage but not as much as along the coast. More...

Shipping and boating off the Carolina coasts is still at considerable risk until Hurricane Fran makes landfall. After landfall the seas should gradually subside, improving conditions for shipping in the area. Rains will carry northward near and east of the Appalachian mountains during the next few days. This will also lead to flooding in another areas not directly impacted by the hurricane.

Tropical depression 8 is mainly a concern for shipping in the region east of the Leeward islands in the south Atlantic during today and Friday. This system may threaten the northeast Caribbean this weekend.
Tropical depression 23w east of the Philippines will mainly be a concern for shipping through the next 72 hours.
